name: tracked-docs-not-clobbered
question: Do any load-bearing tracked docs (CLAUDE.md, root README.md, docs/specs/*.md) contain raw dev-server / build log output (ANSI escape sequences, Vite/cargo/tauri/webpack banners) -- the signature of a misdirected dev-server stdout redirect clobbering a source file?

assertion.asserts: no load-bearing tracked doc has been clobbered by a misdirected dev-server / build stdout redirect
assertion.measures: per scanned file, whether its content contains a literal ANSI CSI escape (the decisive signal) OR at least two of a fixed list of known build-tool banner patterns (Vite/cargo/tauri/webpack)
known_gaps: signature-bound, both ways: a clobber by a tool whose output carries NO ANSI escapes and none of the listed banners passes silently -- the known false-GREEN direction. Adding a new build tool to the project should mean adding its banner signature here

the two-banner threshold is a false-positive guard, not a correctness property: a doc that legitimately QUOTES one build banner (a troubleshooting runbook) is correctly ignored, but one quoting two is reported. Prose about build output is the false-RED direction

the decisive ANSI path has a portability history: it was `grep -qP` until 2026-07-19, which errors on BSD/macOS grep and silently fell through to the weaker banner heuristic while the self-test stayed green (an OVALID-03 instance in this very oracle). It is now `LC_ALL=C grep -qF` with an ANSI-only self-test sample that fails loudly if the decisive path regresses
scope is the configured tracked-doc set: a clobbered file outside it is invisible, not passing

cost_provenance: measured 2026-06-12 on the ULDF framework repo under Git Bash (win32; slowest supported environment) -- pessimistic-honest per ORACLE-COST-01; under-declaration causes timeout kills

contaminated.path: string (repo-relative path of the clobbered doc)
contaminated.ansi: boolean (true if raw ANSI escape sequences were found)
contaminated.excerpt: string (first offending line, ESC bytes shown as <ESC>)

fallback: Open CLAUDE.md / README.md / docs/specs/*.md and look for raw terminal output: ANSI escapes, a `VITE vX.Y ready in N ms` banner, `Compiling <crate> v...`, `Running BeforeDevCommand`, or `webpack compiled`. If present, the file was clobbered by a dev server launched with stdout redirected into it; restore from HEAD (`git show HEAD:<file> > <file>`) and kill any orphaned dev process still holding the file handle (on Windows the handle blocks `git checkout` / `rm` until the process dies).

provenance.note: Starter Verification Oracle. Originated from a reference-implementation incident: a detached dev server launched with stdout redirected into a tracked file (`> CLAUDE.md`) destroyed the file, re-clobbering it on every HMR reload via an inherited file descriptor, and was caught only by chance at the pre-commit diff stage. Makes the catch deterministic and every-finalize (Probandurgy inner-loop gate). The companion mitigation is a one-line guardrail in project CLAUDE.md: never redirect a dev server into a tracked file; log to a gitignored path. v1.1.0 (2026-07-20, upstreamed from a downstream consumer that hit the bug on macOS): run.sh detected ANSI escapes with `grep -qP`, whose PCRE flag BSD/macOS grep lacks -- the check errored out and silently fell through to the weaker textual-banner path, while --self-test stayed falsely green because its only sample also carried banners. Fixed with `LC_ALL=C grep -qF` (portable fixed-string) and guarded by a second ANSI-ONLY self-test sample (in both run.sh and run.ps1) that no banner pattern can match, so a regression of the decisive path now fails the self-test loudly.

config.comment: Scan scope. The run scripts use these defaults; edit the script constants to change scope. Keep the <2s speed contract (Part 11) -- avoid adding large recursive trees.
